title: One-way permutations from one-way functions
formal: Does the existence of a classical one-way function secure against every nonuniform polynomial-size classical adversary imply the existence of an efficiently generated public-key family of one-way permutations on full Boolean cubes, with the same adversary convention? Require a bijection on the entire cube for every key the generator can output, and negligible inversion probability averaged over an honestly generated public key and a uniform input. No trapdoor is required.

title: One-way functions from errorless average-case NP hardness
formal: Is the following implication true? \[(\mathrm{NP},\mathrm{PSamp})\not\subseteq\mathrm{AvgP}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{there exists a classical one-way function}.\] Here the antecedent means that some fixed NP language, under some fixed polynomial-time samplable distribution ensemble, has no deterministic exact decider with average polynomial running time in the moment sense below. The conclusion asks for a total polynomial-time computable function \(f:\{0,1\}^{*}\to\{0,1\}^{*}\) such that, for every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time inverter \(I\) and every integer \(c\ge1\), there exists \(n_0\) for which, for every \(n\ge n_0\), \[\Pr_{x\sim U_n,\ I}\bigl[|z|=n\ \land\ f(z)=f(x)\bigr]\le n^{-c},\qquad z\leftarrow I(1^n,f(x)).\] The statement is unrelativized and has no additional hardness, derandomization or cryptographic assumption.

title: Witness encryption from plain LWE
formal: Assuming the specified polynomial-modulus decisional LWE hardness, does every polynomial-time NP witness relation admit standard-model witness encryption with correctness for valid witnesses and message indistinguishability on false instances?

title: General functional encryption from plain LWE
formal: Does the specified ordinary decisional LWE assumption imply public-key functional encryption for all polynomial-size Boolean circuits, with adaptive indistinguishability security against arbitrarily polynomially many colluding functional-key queries?

title: Optimal error for pure-DP continual counting
formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors as \(T\to \infty , E(T)=\inf _{M} \max _{x\in \{0,1\}^{T}} E_{Y\sim M_{x}}[\max _{1\le t\le T}|Y_{t}- \sum_{i=1}^{t} x_{i}|]\), where the infimum is over all causal \((1/2,0)\)-differentially private mechanisms defined below.

title: Pseudorandom functions from worst-case hardness of learning
formal:
For every circuit class
\[
\mathcal C\in\{\mathrm{AC}^0,\ \mathrm{AC}^0[p]\ (p\text{ any fixed prime}),\
\mathrm{ACC}^0,\ \mathrm{TC}^0,\ \mathrm{NC}^1,\
\mathrm{Formula},\ \mathrm{Circuit}\},
\]
does the following implication hold?
\[
\neg\operatorname{Learn}_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathcal C)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{PRF}_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathcal C).
\]
Here learning means uniform randomized polynomial-time improper learning under the uniform input distribution, with adaptive membership queries. The conclusion is a uniformly polynomial-time samplable family of functions computed by polynomial-size \(\mathcal C\)-circuits, secure against every uniform probabilistic polynomial-time oracle distinguisher. Both notions are defined below.

The hypothesis is only worst-case failure of learning: each candidate learner may fail on its own target function. No efficiently samplable common distribution of hard targets is assumed.

title: Unbounded fully homomorphic encryption from polynomial-factor GapSVP
formal: Does there exist a classical compact fully homomorphic public-key encryption scheme, with keys generated without any circuit-depth bound, and an integer \(a\ge1\), such that there is a quantum polynomial-time reduction from solving worst-case Euclidean \(\mathrm{GapSVP}_{n^a}\) to breaking its chosen-plaintext security, in the precise sense below? The scheme must support every polynomial-size Boolean circuit using the same key-generation algorithm. No independent circular-security or other cryptographic assumption may be used. A quantum reduction is permitted, while key generation, encryption, homomorphic evaluation and decryption are classical.

title: One-way functions in \(\mathrm{NC}^{0}\) from one-way functions
formal:
Does the existence of a classical one-way function imply the existence of a classical one-way function computed by a polynomial-time uniform \(\mathrm{NC}^{0}\) circuit family? With the definitions below, the proposition is
\[
\bigl[\exists f\;\mathrm{OWF}(f)\bigr]
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\bigl[\exists g\;\mathrm{OWF}(g)\land\mathrm{PUniformNC}^{0}(g)\bigr].
\]
Both sides require security against every nonuniform polynomial-size classical circuit family. The conclusion asks for the existence of some such \(g\), with some constant depth and some polynomial bounds. These constants may depend on \(g\), but not on its input length or on an adversary. There is no additional assumption on the starting function's circuit depth, no requirement that \(f\) and \(g\) have the same input or output lengths, and no requirement of a black-box construction or an efficient compiler from descriptions of \(f\).

title: Optimal regret for private stochastic online learning
formal: Determine, up to universal constant factors, the optimal expected pseudo-regret \(R^{*}(K,T,\varepsilon,\Delta)\) for pure differentially private stochastic full-information online learning. The domain is integers \(K\ge2\), \(T\ge1\), and real parameters \(\varepsilon>0\), \(0<\Delta\le1\). For independent loss distributions \(P_1,\ldots,P_K\) on \([0,1]\), let \(\mu_j=\mathbb E_{P_j}[L]\); require a unique minimizer \(j^{*}\) and \(\mu_j-\mu_{j^{*}}\ge\Delta\) for every \(j\ne j^{*}\). At round \(t\), select \(I_t\in[K]\) using only earlier observations and private randomness, incur loss \(L_{I_t,t}\), and then observe the entire vector \(L_t\), where all \(L_{j,t}\sim P_j\) are independent across actions and rounds. Put \[R^{*}(K,T,\varepsilon,\Delta)=\inf_A\sup_{(P_1,\ldots,P_K)}\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^{T}(\mu_{I_t}-\mu_{j^{*}})\right],\] where the supremum ranges over the promised product distributions and the infimum over the causal \(\varepsilon\)-private strategies defined below. The requested rate retains every dependence on \(K,T,\varepsilon,\Delta\), including logarithmic factors and the small-horizon regime.

title: Identity-based encryption from arbitrary public-key encryption
formal: Does the existence of IND-CPA-secure public-key bit encryption imply an adaptively IND-ID-CPA-secure identity-based bit-encryption scheme for identity space \(\{0,1\}^{\lambda}\) with polynomial-size public parameters, under the classical standard-model conventions below?

title: Dual pseudorandom functions from arbitrary one-way functions
formal: Does the existence of arbitrary one-way functions imply a uniformly efficiently computable dual pseudorandom function family F_lambda:{0,1}^lambda × {0,1}^lambda to {0,1}^lambda with adaptive oracle security in each orientation?

title: Constant-round concurrent zero knowledge from LWE alone
formal: Does the specified ordinary LWE assumption imply a constant-round plain-model concurrent zero-knowledge argument for every NP relation, with no a priori bound on polynomially many interleaved sessions and with expected-polynomial-time simulation?

title: Exponentially hard weak versus strong one-way functions
formal: Does the existence of an exponentially hard weak one-way function imply the existence of an exponentially hard strong one-way function, in the following nonuniform-adversary, negligible-success formulation? The premise is that there exist a uniform polynomial-time computable length-preserving function \(f\), a real \(a>0\), an integer \(k\ge1\), and \(n_0\), such that \[\operatorname{Inv}_f(C,n)\le1-n^{-k}\] for every \(n\ge n_0\) and every circuit \(C\) with \(n\) inputs, \(n\) outputs and at most \(2^{an}\) gates. The desired conclusion is that there exist another uniform polynomial-time computable length-preserving function \(g\) and a real \(b>0\) such that, for every integer \(d\ge1\), there is \(n_d\) with \[\operatorname{Inv}_g(C,n)\le n^{-d}\] for every \(n\ge n_d\) and every such circuit with at most \(2^{bn}\) gates. The constants and function in the conclusion may depend on those witnessing the premise.

title: Linear-seed pseudorandom generators from one-way functions
formal:
Can every efficiently evaluable length-preserving one-way function be converted into a fully explicit pseudorandom generator with seed length linear in the function's input length, while retaining the following quantitative security?

Precisely, for every integer \(b\ge1\), do there exist integers \(A,K,q,r\ge1\), \(\ell_0\ge4\), and one deterministic compiler \(\mathcal B_b\) such that the following holds? Its input is a Boolean circuit \(F:\{0,1\}^{\ell}\to\{0,1\}^{\ell}\) of size at most \(\ell^b\), integers \(\ell\ge\ell_0\), \(1\le s\le2^{2\ell}\), \(m>A\ell\), and \(1\le e\le2\ell\). Write
\[
 \varepsilon=2^{-e},\qquad
 t=\left\lfloor\frac{s}{K(m2^e)^q}\right\rfloor,
\]
and require \(t\ge1\). Suppose every inversion circuit \(I\) of size at most \(s\) satisfies
\[
 \Pr_{x\leftarrow U_{\ell}}[F(I(F(x)))=F(x)]\le\frac12.
\]
The compiler must produce a circuit \(G:\{0,1\}^{d}\to\{0,1\}^{m}\), with \(1\le d\le A\ell<m\), in at most \(K(m+1)^r\) bit operations, such that every Boolean distinguishing circuit \(T\) of size at most \(t\) satisfies
\[
 \left|\Pr[T(G(U_d))=1]-\Pr[T(U_m)=1]\right|\le\varepsilon.
\]
The construction may depend on \(s\) and \(\varepsilon\): a separate generator is permitted for each requested pair of these parameters.

title: Optimal private sample complexity for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization
formal: Editorial zero-order variant: determine the sample complexity of uniformly polynomial-time central \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-private algorithms returning \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with \[\mathbb E\,\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial_\alpha F(X))\le\beta\] for all population objectives in the normalized class below. Determine matching upper and lower bounds up to factors polynomial in \(\log(2+d+1/\alpha+1/\beta+1/\varepsilon+1/\delta)\). Expectation includes the independent dataset and algorithm randomness.

title: Subpolynomial-key perfectly secure three-server DPFs
formal: Does there exist a fixed finite Abelian group \(G\), with \(|G|\ge2\), and a uniform three-server distributed point function with perfect correctness, perfect privacy against any one server, and worst-case key length \(\ell(N)=N^{o(1)}\)? For every integer \(N\ge2\), location \(\alpha\in[N]\), and value \(\beta\in G\), key generation must produce three binary keys \((k_0,k_1,k_2)\) such that \[\sum_{i=0}^{2}\operatorname{Eval}_i(k_i,x)=\begin{cases}\beta&x=\alpha,\\0_G&x\ne\alpha\end{cases}\qquad\text{for every }x\in[N]\] with probability one. For each individual \(i\), the distribution of \(k_i\) must be identical for all pairs \((\alpha,\beta)\) with the same \(N\). Every generated key must have at most \(\ell(N)\) bits. The fixed output group may be chosen as part of a positive answer; requiring all output groups is the source's separate question.

title: Unconditional zero knowledge for gap circuit complexity
formal: Is there a fixed rational \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)\) for which \(\mathrm{Gap}_{\varepsilon}\mathrm{MCSP}\) admits a computational zero-knowledge interactive proof system without a computational hardness assumption? Given the length-\(N=2^n\) truth table of a Boolean function, the promise distinguishes circuit size at most \(N^\varepsilon\) from size greater than \(N^{1-\varepsilon}\). This card selects the MCSP branch of the original question and the gap family used by Hirahara and Nanashima; it does not claim equivalence with every MINKT or other gap variant.
